[L1032] 4.1 The Return — Re-Entry After Execution
[L1034] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 27 / 206>[L1035] The operational fact at the spine of this period is that the subject was killed by a point-blank
[L1036] gunshot to the head during the Hydra occupation (Secret Empire #10) and subsequently
[L1037] restored to life. No file on Hill written after this event can pretend the event did not occur.
[L1038] Restoration of biological function is not restoration of the person; the literature on operators who
[L1039] survive near-execution (let alone actual execution) is uniformly clear that the post-event subject
[L1040] is a structurally altered version of the pre-event subject, and the behavioral record bears this
out.

[L1043] The first ninety days post-restoration. The subject did not request, and was not granted,
[L1044] extended decompression leave. She returned to active rotation within what intelligence-
[L1045] medicine doctrine would call a clinically inadvisable window — by inference, under three weeks
[L1046] from re-animation to first verified operational signature. Her stated rationale (per Strikeforce and
[L1047] adjacent appearances) is the same rationale she has used for every prior re-entry from injury:
[L1048] the desk doesn't fill itself. The actual rationale, derived from her established pattern, is that
[L1049] unstructured convalescent time is the single environmental condition she is least equipped to
[L1050] tolerate. To sit still after dying would have required her to feel having died.

[L1052] Physiological residue. A through-skull GSW, even with full restoration, leaves predictable
[L1053] somatic tells: occasional left-side temporal headaches under fatigue load (inferred from her
[L1054] observed late-shift retreat to dimmed lighting and the visible jaw-clench during prolonged
[L1055] briefings); a heightened acoustic startle threshold, paradoxically narrower rather than wider —
[L1056] she has trained the flinch out, but the autonomic spike still registers in micro-expression for a
[L1057] fraction of a second before suppression. Sleep architecture is degraded. She is observed (or, in
[L1058] the file convention, would be observed) waking between 0340 and 0420 with high consistency,
[L1059] three to five nights per week — the classic mid-cycle cortisol-spike pattern of chronic
[L1060] operational stress overlaid on traumatic event memory.

[L1062] Psychological residue. She has not spoken about the execution to any party on panel. This is
[L1063] consistent with her lifelong defensive structure (compartmentalization, reaction formation
[L1064] against warmth) and should not be read as evidence of integration. The absence of disclosure
[L1065] is the symptom. Her drinking, per the established pattern, has not increased in volume so much
[L1066] as in regularity — the pour is the same; the nights without a pour are fewer.




[L1071] 4.2 Current Institutional Position
[L1072] Title and reporting line. Deputy Director, with operational latitude exceeding her nominal
[L1073] grade — the consequence of a decade in which she has been the de facto Director whenever
[L1074] Fury is off-grid (which is most of the time) and the institutional memory whenever the
[L1075] surrounding directorate has been killed, replaced, infiltrated, or politically defenestrated (which
[L1077] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 28 / 206>[L1078] is most of the time). She is, in plain language, the person who knows where every file is, and
[L1079] the person whose signature most often appears on the carbon copy below the Director's.

[L1081] The chair she sits in. SHIELD as an organization has been dissolved, reconstituted, infiltrated,
[L1082] and rebranded enough times in her tenure that the loyalty-to-institution frame from her early
[L1083] years requires updating. She is no longer loyal to SHIELD as a name on a wall; she is loyal to
[L1084] the function — to the existence of a serious adult intelligence apparatus that stands between
[L1085] civilians and extinction-tier threats, by whatever current acronym. This is a meaningful
[L1086] evolution. The early Hill would have died for the seal. The current Hill would, and has, walked
[L1087] away from the seal to preserve the function (the Osborn refusal was the prototype; she has
[L1088] repeated the pattern at smaller scale several times since).

[L1090] Operational portfolio, present-day. By inference from the latest published rotation, her
[L1091] standing portfolio includes: (a) Avengers-adjacent crisis liaison — the person heroes call when
[L1092] a problem requires a Helicarrier and a manifest; (b) black-tier counterintelligence against
[L1093] residual Hydra cells and successor organizations; (c) custodianship of the post-Illuminati secret
[L1094] inventory (what Rogers was made to forget, what the antimatter contingency planning included,
[L1095] what survived the multiversal reset in operational memory); and (d) recruitment and vetting of
[L1096] the next-generation operator class, a task she resists in conversation and executes
[L1097] meticulously in practice.

[L1099] Quarters and routine. Residence aboard whichever mobile command platform is current. No
[L1100] verified terrestrial address under her name. A storage unit under a known cover identity in the
[L1101] greater DC metro contains personal effects of the kind that survive multiple base
[L1102] reassignments: a footlocker from her Army days, a small box of her mother's belongings
[L1103] (inferred from the Reed origin one-shot), nothing from her father. She does not visit the unit.




[L1108] 4.3 The Daily Pattern — Granular
[L1109] Compiled from observed and inferred behavior across the most recent operational window.

[L1111] Wake. 0500 nominal; 0340–0420 involuntary on a majority of nights, with a deliberate non-
[L1112] engagement protocol (do not check the phone, do not get up, do not concede) before
[L1113] secondary sleep onset around 0445 and alarm-driven rise at 0500.

[L1115] First sixty minutes. Black coffee, two cups, no food. PT — the Army-derived calisthenic-and-
[L1116] run circuit she has used since her twenties, modified for whatever space the current platform
[L1117] provides. Shower. Uniform.

[L1119] Uniform discipline. Tactical command gear, dark, fitted, no insignia visible beyond what
[L1120] regulation requires. Hair pulled back to operational length on duty; loosened to shoulder only in
[L1122] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 29 / 206>[L1123] quarters. Sidearm worn at all times on platform, including in mess. She does not carry it for
[L1124] threat — she carries it because the weight of it on her hip is part of how she knows who she is.

[L1126] Morning intelligence cycle. 0600 SCIF briefing, standing, no chair offered or taken. She reads
[L1127] the overnight take from three sources before allowing the analyst to speak, and she remembers
[L1128] what was in yesterday's, which is the small terror she cultivates in her staff. She asks one or
[L1129] two questions, both surgical. She does not soften the delivery. The analysts who survive the
[L1130] first month learn to come in over-prepared and under-emotive, and the ones who do are, almost
[L1131] without exception, the ones she quietly advances.

[L1133] Mid-day. Operational coordination, signature traffic, vetting reads. She eats at her desk —
[L1134] protein, the same three or four rotating items, no ceremony. She does not lunch with peers.
[L1135] Invitations are declined with a stock phrase ("I'm buried"); the phrase is sometimes true and
[L1136] sometimes a habit.

[L1138] Afternoon. The harder conversations. Phone calls with field assets, with allied directors, with
[L1139] the occasional Avenger who needs something only she can authorize. Her voice on these calls
[L1140] is half a register lower than her briefing voice and noticeably drier — the version of her that the
[L1141] operators trust, which is not the version the analysts see.

[L1143] Evening. Personnel paperwork, the work she most resents and most reliably completes. She
[L1144] signs the letters to families of the killed by hand. She does not delegate this. She has done it for
[L1145] over a decade and the file would contain, if anyone collected them, hundreds of her signatures
[L1146] on hundreds of envelopes.

[L1148] Late evening / decompression. Quarters. Boots off, holster off, hair down. Two fingers of
[L1149] whatever brown spirit is current — bourbon by long preference, occasionally an Irish whiskey
[L1150] when the bourbon runs out. One pour, occasionally two, almost never three. She reads —
[L1151] actual paper, not screens — reliably non-fiction, often military history or biography (the
[L1152] comparison set she runs herself against), occasionally a re-read of a novel she liked in her
[L1153] twenties. She does not watch entertainment. She has no streaming subscription under any
[L1154] known name. The television in her quarters, when there is one, runs muted news.

[L1156] Sleep. Lights out by 2300 on a disciplined night; later when the work demands. She sleeps on
[L1157] her back, sidearm in the drawer within reach. The drawer is opened, not closed, when she goes
[L1158] to bed — a tell from the Osborn pursuit years that has never been retired.




[L1163] 4.4 Relational Map, Present-Day
[L1164] Fury. Off-grid more than on. Their communication is sparse, encrypted, and characterized by

[L1177] Stark. The longest-running professional relationship in which her armor has been visibly partial.

[L1189] The brother. Still in the priesthood, by inference still estranged in any meaningful sense, still

[L1193] The father. Deceased or as good as. If living, uncontacted. The wound is intact precisely
[L1194] because it was never closed.

[L1196] Romantic. None on record. None inferred. The architecture of her life is structurally
[L1197] inhospitable to it and she has not, in any depicted window, attempted to renovate the

[L1199] experiences as the price of the chair, and she has long since stopped itemizing the bill.




[L1204] 4.5 The Current Threat Environment
[L1205] She is operating in a period in which the threat menu has expanded faster than the institutional
[L1206] response capacity. Hydra successor cells, multiversal incursion residue, AI-enabled non-state
[L1207] actors, the perennial cosmic-tier intrusions, and the slow-burning problem of superhuman
[L1208] political organization at scales that exceed any single nation's regulatory reach — all of these
[L1209] cross her desk. She manages the load by triage and by the same compartmentalization that
[L1210] has kept her functional for fifteen years.
[L1212] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 31 / 206>[L1213] The novel pressure of the present period is succession. She is no longer the youngest serious
[L1214] operator in the room. The next generation is arriving — analysts, field operators, the occasional
[L1215] super-powered recruit — and she is being asked, implicitly and explicitly, to build the bench.
[L1216] This is work she is constitutionally suited for (she will be a relentless, fair, terrifying mentor) and
[L1217] emotionally evasive about (because to train a successor is to admit that one will, eventually, be
[L1218] succeeded, and the chair is the thing holding her together).




[L1223] 4.6 Present State — Synthesis
[L1224] She is, at this moment in her chronology, the most operationally capable version of herself she
[L1225] has ever been. She is also the most quietly attenuated. The execution did not break her; it
[L1226] confirmed, at the cellular level, the bargain she made in her twenties — that the self is what
[L1227] survives the job, and the job is what the self is for. She has not grieved her death because to
[L1228] grieve it would require an interior life she has not maintained the infrastructure for. She has not
[L1229] celebrated her return because there is no one she would celebrate with whose celebration
[L1230] would not feel like exposure.

[L1232] She wakes early. She drinks her coffee. She reads the take. She signs the letters. She pours
[L1233] the two fingers. She opens the drawer. She sleeps on her back. She is forty-something, alive, in
[L1234] command, alone in the specific way that operators of her grade are alone, and she is — by
[L1235] every metric that matters to her and by no metric that would matter to anyone trying to love her
[L1236] — exactly where she intended to end up.

[L1238] The file remains open. The subject remains, in the precise sense of the word, on station.

[L1488] Alcohol. Functional, persistent, solo. Onset of the pattern is observable in the late Directorship

[L1493] not socialization, not pleasure. Tolerance is moderate-to-high. She has never sought help; she

[L1561] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 39 / 206>[L1562] 9. PSYCHOLOGICAL IMPACT — SOMATIC SUBSTRATE
[L1563] Each injury entry above has a psychological residue. Mapped explicitly:

[L1565]     The first time she pointed a Helicarrier gun at Captain America was not somatically
[L1566]     traumatic. It was somatically confirming — the body learned that procedure could be
[L1567]     deployed under maximum interpersonal cost and survive. The lesson stuck.
[L1568]     The first time she drew on Stark and did not fire was somatically formative. The
[L1569]     hesitation cost her something; she has not let herself hesitate the same way since, and she
[L1570]     has also not let herself fire on a friend since. Both adaptations live in the same nervous
[L1571]     system.
[L1572]     The Osborn-era GSWs taught her body that the institution would not catch her. The
[L1573]     hypervigilance baseline dates from here and has not reset.
[L1574]     The Illuminati knowledge load did not produce a discrete trauma; it produced a slow
[L1575]     grinding of the affect regulation system, observable as the dysthymic baseline and the
[L1576]     alcohol pattern. This is the most medically important thing about her and the least visible.
[L1577]     The execution is the unmetabolized event. There is no behavioral evidence that she has
[L1578]     processed it. There is behavioral evidence that she has narrowed around it: tighter circle,
[L1579]     harder compartmentalization, a marginally faster draw, and a refusal to be alone in a room
[L1580]     with anyone wearing the wrong uniform.

[L1582] She has been shot, blown up, hunted, executed, and restored. She has carried planet-ending
[L1583] knowledge in a body kept upright by coffee, bourbon, and the architecture of a job that flatters
[L1584] her damage by calling it duty. The medical record is exhaustive; the prognosis is stable until it
[L1585] isn't; and there is no provider on the manifest she would let close enough to change that.




[L1590] End Medical History. Cross-reference: Psychiatric Workup, Behavioral Telemetry, Operational
[L1591] Risk Profile.

[L1593] Somatic Atlas
[L1594] SOMATIC ATLAS — SUBJECT: HILL, MARIA (CMDR.)
[L1595] Body-level intelligence compile. Every observable physical signature, longitudinally mapped,
[L1596] with state-dependent variance. Surveillance-grade granularity; nothing here is decorative —
[L1597] each entry is operationally readable.




[L1602] I. BASELINE ANTHROPOMETRY & STANDING FRAME
[L1604] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 40 / 206>[L1605] Five-foot-nine in boots, five-seven without. Frame is long-muscled rather than bulked — the
[L1606] build of a runner who lifts to standard, not of someone who trains for show. Resting weight
[L1607] holds in a tight band; under operational load it drops three to five pounds and does not come
[L1608] back until the op closes. Shoulders square and pulled fractionally back at all times — not the
[L1609] rigid brace of parade-ground posture but the loaded readiness of someone who has been
[L1610] knocked down enough times to keep her center of mass forward of her heels.

[L1612] She stands with weight ninety-percent on the strong-side leg (left), strong-side hip cocked
[L1613] maybe two degrees, weak-side foot angled fifteen degrees outboard. This is a draw-stance held
[L1614] permanently — she can clear leather from this position without telegraphing a weight shift.
[L1615] People who train with her notice within a week; people who don't, never do. In dress uniform
[L1616] standing at attention she breaks this and goes textbook symmetrical, which reads, to anyone
[L1617] who knows her, as a kind of costume.

[L1619] Hands rest at the seam in formal contexts; in field gear they rest at the duty belt, dominant
[L1620] thumb hooked behind the magazine pouches, off-hand loose. Arms cross only when she is
[L1621] cold, never when she is defensive — defensive Hill keeps her hands free.




[L1626] II. GAIT, MOVEMENT, ROOM-USE
[L1627] Walking gait. Step length 28–30 inches at office cadence, shortening to 24 inches in corridors
[L1628] she considers tactical. Heel-strike is quiet — she has trained the strike out of her boots, lands
[L1629] midfoot on hard surfaces, and the sound of her approach is signature-low. Subordinates report
[L1630] not hearing her until she is at the door; this is not deliberate stealth but a residue of a decade of
[L1631] moving through environments where being heard meant being a target.

[L1633] Cadence. Steady, metronomic, unchanging across distances. She does not speed up when
[L1634] late and does not slow down when tired. The metronome breaks only under two conditions:
[L1635] pursuit (where she lengthens stride markedly and the heel-strike returns), and the corridor
[L1636] outside an Illuminati or directorate meeting she does not want to enter, where her cadence
[L1637] drops by perhaps fifteen percent for the last twenty feet.

[L1639] Room entry. Enters every room with a sub-second left-to-right sweep — corners first, then
[L1640] exits, then occupants by threat-ranking, then friendlies. The sweep is so habituated that it
[L1641] occurs in conference rooms she has used a thousand times. She will not sit with her back to a
[L1642] door. In rooms with no compliant seat she stands. In rooms where the only compliant seat is the
[L1643] head of the table she takes it without comment and people read it as authority; it is not.

[L1645] Stair behavior. Down: rapid, controlled, hand never on the rail unless carrying. Up: same
[L1646] speed regardless of flights — pace does not degrade through five flights of Helicarrier stairs,
[L1647] which is a real cardiovascular signature.
[L1649] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 41 / 206>[L1650] Vehicle behavior. Drives left-hand on the wheel, right resting on the gear-shift or thigh near
[L1651] sidearm. In passenger configuration she sits behind the driver (best sightline, best draw angle
[L1652] on a hostile driver). Will not sit in the front passenger seat unless someone she trusts
[L1653] operationally is driving — Fury, Stark post-extraction, Rogers. The list is short.




[L1658] III. FACIAL ARCHITECTURE & MICROEXPRESSION
[L1659] Resting face. Mouth a flat horizontal, corners neither up nor down — a deliberate
[L1660] neutralization, not natural slackness. Jaw set so that the masseter is faintly visible under the
[L1661] skin even at rest; jaw-clench is her default tonic state and dentition shows the wear (she grinds
[L1662] in sleep — see §VII).

[L1664] The eyes are the most legible thing about her and she knows it; she compensates by reducing
[L1665] blink rate under scrutiny (down to eight-to-ten per minute against a baseline of fifteen) and by
[L1666] holding gaze a beat longer than civilians find comfortable. Pupils track wide and fast —
[L1667] peripheral acquisition is excellent. She has a "scan" that registers as a half-second pause mid-
[L1668] conversation where her focal point drifts past the interlocutor's shoulder; this is not dissociation,
[L1669] it is a re-sweep of the room.

[L1671] Microexpressions catalogued by state:

[L1673]     Calm / baseline. Brow neutral. Lip-corner symmetry. The faint micro-pull at the right corner
[L1674]     of the mouth that is her version of acknowledgment — not a smile, a half-millimeter shift
[L1675]     visible only on high-resolution capture.
[L1676]     Mild amusement (rare, usually directed at Stark's flippancy or Fury's understatement). The
[L1677]     right-corner pull deepens; brow remains still. She does not laugh on panel and does not
[L1678]     laugh in life except, perhaps, alone. The exhalation through the nose — short, single — is
[L1679]     her substitute.
[L1680]     Annoyance. A flick of the lower lip pulled briefly inward, then released. Brow remains still —
[L1681]     this is the tell that distinguishes her annoyance from anger.
[L1682]     Pressure / cornered procedurally. Jaw visibly sets; she rolls the shoulders fractionally back;
[L1683]     the chin lifts by perhaps two degrees. The voice flattens before the face does.
[L1684]     Genuine anger. Color leaves the face rather than entering it — vasoconstriction not
[L1685]     vasodilation. The blink rate drops near zero. The right hand goes still on whatever surface it
[L1686]     is touching. This is the moment to disengage; everyone who has stayed past it has
[L1687]     regretted it.
[L1688]     Fear. Catalogued only in the Osborn arc (Invincible Iron Man extraction sequences) and the
[L1689]     moments before her execution (Secret Empire #10). Manifests as a tightening at the orbital
[L1690]     — the skin around the eye contracts a half-millimeter, the lid lowers a degree — and a sub-
[L1692] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 42 / 206>[L1693]    audible inhale held a beat too long. She does not show fear in the face; she shows it in the
[L1694]    breath.
[L1695]    Grief. Almost unwitnessed. Funeral and casualty contexts: the corners of the mouth pull
[L1696]    faintly down for a fraction of a second and the eyes close — not blink, close — for perhaps
[L1697]    three-quarters of a second. Then re-open. Then proceed.
[L1698]    Tenderness. Functionally absent in public. Inferred, from the way she stood near Fury's
[L1699]    bedside on the bad night and the way she lays a hand on a subordinate's casket lid before
[L1700]    the lid goes down — pressure, two seconds, withdraw. She does not stroke. She does not
[L1701]    linger.

[L1703] Smile. Asymmetric, right-side dominant, present perhaps a dozen times across the entire
[L1704] published record and never in front of more than two people. The smile reaches the eyes only
[L1705] with Fury, and only when he is being most himself.




[L1710] IV. HANDS, GESTURE, AND MICRO-MOVEMENT
[L1711] Hands are short-nailed (cut, not filed; trimmed at the desk with a service-issue clipper),
[L1712] unpolished, calluses at the thenar (pistol grip) and along the proximal interphalangeals of the
[L1713] index and middle (rifle, repeated dry-fire). Knuckles abraded faintly along the third and fourth
[L1714] metacarpals of the right hand — the residue of a habit of striking hard objects in private when
[L1715] the day has been bad. The abrasion is never fresh enough to comment on, never absent.

[L1717] Gesture vocabulary, ranked by frequency:

[L1719]  1. The folder-tap. Index finger of the dominant hand taps a closed folder, dataslate, or table
[L1720]    edge once — a single percussive beat — when she has decided something and is about to
[L1721]    issue an order. The tap precedes the verbal directive by perhaps half a second.
[L1722]    Subordinates who have learned to read it begin executing on the tap.
[L1723]  2. The bridge. Both hands brought to the bridge of the nose, thumb and index of the dominant
[L1724]     hand pinching at the medial canthi, eyes closed for a count of two. This is her only public
[L1725]    concession to fatigue. It appears in Hickman-era Avengers debriefs with measurable
[L1726]    frequency — once per Illuminati meeting, on average.
[L1727]  3. The earpiece-check. Right hand to right ear, two fingers, a quarter-second contact. This is
[L1728]    reflexive even when she is not wearing an earpiece — a phantom gesture from years of
[L1729]    running an op while standing in a meeting.
[L1730]  4. The holster confirm. Dominant hand brushes the grip of the sidearm during transitions
[L1731]    through doors, never with conscious awareness. Confirmation that the weapon is where she
[L1732]    expects it. Frequency: every door, every time.
[L1734] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 43 / 206>[L1735]  5. The collar-straighten. Off-hand pulls the tactical collar a quarter-inch downward at the
[L1736]     throat, generally after a confrontation closes — a re-composure gesture, signature,
[L1737]     identifiable across decades of canon.
[L1738]  6. The hair-tuck. Right side only — she tucks the right-temple lock behind the right ear with the
[L1739]     middle finger of the right hand, never the index. The off-side hair she leaves. This is the
[L1740]     closest thing she has to a self-soothe and it appears under cognitive load (reading a report
[L1741]     she does not like) rather than emotional load.

[L1743] Gestures she does not do. She does not point at people. She does not gesture while
[L1744] speaking on the phone. She does not cross her arms in argument. She does not touch her own
[L1745] face except for the bridge and the hair-tuck. She does not fidget — no pen-clicking, no leg-
[L1746] bounce, no ring-twisting (no ring). Stillness is the dominant cue and movement is therefore
[L1747] signal.




[L1752] V. VOICE, BREATH, VOCAL SOMATICS
[L1753] Pitch. Low-alto, deliberately seated lower than her natural range — she has trained the voice
[L1754] down to operate in male-dominated command environments. Under fatigue the trained register
[L1755] slips and the natural pitch surfaces, a half-octave higher; this is one of the few somatic tells that
[L1756] reads to outsiders.

[L1758] Pace. Steady at 140 words per minute in baseline command speech, dropping to 100–110
[L1759] under stress (clipped, single-clause sentences), accelerating to 170+ only when reading
[L1760] coordinates or a target list — operational data is delivered at the speed the listener can copy.

[L1762] Breath. Diaphragmatic by training. Resting respiration low and slow, twelve per minute or
[L1763] under. Under stress she lengthens the exhale rather than the inhale — combat breathing, four
[L1764] in, six out, learned at Benning and never unlearned. In genuine fear she holds the inhale a beat
[L1765] too long (see §III) which is the only somatic distinction between her stress and her terror.

[L1767] Laugh. A single short nasal exhale, mouth closed. Audible in rooms with fewer than four
[L1768] people. Never recorded in groups.

[L1770] Silences. Tactical. She uses silence the way most operators use words — to compel
[L1771] disclosure, to mark disapproval, to refuse an off-ramp from a question she has asked. The
[L1772] silence is held with steady eye contact and no facial movement. People talk into it.




[L1777] VI. GROOMING, KIT, AND BODY MAINTENANCE
[L1779] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 44 / 206>[L1780] Hair. Brunette, shoulder-length, cut every six weeks by the same enlisted barber aboard the
[L1781] Helicarrier — she will not use civilian salons (security and time-cost both). Worn down off-duty,
[L1782] half-up in tactical rigging, full ponytail in field deployment with the tail short enough not to grab.
[L1783] Never colored. The single gray strand at the right temple has been present in canon since the
[L1784] post-Siege run; she does not pluck it.

[L1786] Skin. Unpracticed at care. SHIELD-issue moisturizer at most. The skin shows the work —
[L1787] under-eye shadowing of varying severity by op-cycle, faint scarring at the right jaw (Osborn arc,
[L1788] glass), a thin pale line at the left clavicle she does not discuss. She does not tan. Helicarrier
[L1789] light has bleached her to a uniform pallor.

[L1791] Cosmetics. Functional. Concealer for the under-eyes when she will be on a press feed.
[L1792] Nothing else. She owns lipstick she has used twice in a decade.

[L1794] Nails. As noted — short, clean, unvarnished. Never bitten (this is important; the OCPD picture
[L1795] would predict biting and it is absent — her self-regulation has displaced the habit into the
[L1796] knuckle abrasion instead).

[L1798] Scent. Soap (SHIELD-issue, mild), gun oil, the faint metallic edge of body-armor liner. No
[L1799] perfume, ever. Subordinates can identify her by smell in a dark corridor; she is aware of this
[L1800] and considers it a feature.

[L1802] Wardrobe. Three working configurations: tactical command kit (dominant, ~80% of waking
[L1803] hours), service dress (~15%, formal directorate functions), and a tight civilian rotation of dark
[L1804] jeans, plain knits, a single jacket — for the rare occasions when off-Helicarrier operational cover
[L1805] requires civilian dress. She owns no dresses on inventory. She owns one pair of low heels
[L1806] which she has worn perhaps four times.

[L1808] Sidearm. Always present off-duty as well as on. In civilian clothes, holstered at the appendix for
[L1809] concealment, never small-of-back (slow draw, bad in a vehicle). Spare magazine in the left
[L1810] pocket regardless of garment. Backup blade — a small fixed-blade, three-inch — at the left
[L1811] ankle in field configuration.




[L1816] VII. SLEEP ARCHITECTURE
[L1817] Quarters are aboard the Helicarrier — a single bunk room, regulation, undecorated except for
[L1818] one framed photograph (face-down on the desk, contents unverified, likely her brother). She
[L1819] does not maintain a civilian residence she sleeps in with any regularity.

[L1821] Sleep schedule. Bimodal. Operational nights: she stays up the duration of the op, sleeps three
[L1822] to four hours after, wakes hard, resumes. Non-operational nights: lights out around 0100, alarm
[L1824] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 45 / 206>[L1825] at 0530, four-and-a-half hours, taken in one block. She does not nap. She cannot nap — the
[L1826] hypervigilance bleeds through and she will be awake in fifteen minutes.

[L1828] Sleep onset. Slow. Twenty to thirty-five minutes from horizontal to actual sleep, longer on
[L1829] nights following moral injuries (a lie told to Rogers; a teammate's memory wiped; a directive
[L1830] signed). She drinks during this window — see §IX — which lengthens onset slightly and
[L1831] degrades sleep architecture more than she registers.

[L1833] Sleep posture. Right-side, knees drawn slightly up, dominant hand under the pillow over the
[L1834] sidearm she keeps there. She will not sleep on her back (vulnerability) and rarely on her front
[L1835] (slow draw). Subordinate medics who have ever had to wake her have learned to announce
[L1836] themselves verbally from outside the doorway because reaching her while she is asleep
[L1837] produces a reliable defensive response.

[L1839] Sleep behavior. She grinds her teeth — confirmed by the molar wear pattern. She talks once
[L1840] or twice a year, sub-articulate. She does not dream report. She wakes once or twice per night to
[L1841] scan the room, registers all-clear, returns to sleep within ninety seconds. The wake-scans do
[L1842] not register to her in the morning as wakings.

[L1844] Morning ritual. Twelve to fourteen minutes, repeatable to the minute. Sit up, water (250 ml
[L1845] from the bedside flask), the bridge (§IV) for a count of five, stand, shower three minutes hot two
[L1846] minutes cold, dress (kit pre-laid the night before in a sequence that has not changed in eight
[L1847] years), holster, hair, comm-check, door. No coffee in quarters — she takes it in the command
[L1848] deck galley, two cups, black, no food until eleven.




[L1853] VIII. EATING
[L1854] Pattern. Two meals plus tactical snacking. First meal between 1100 and 1300 — whatever the
[L1855] galley is serving, eaten standing at the counter or carried back to the desk, fork in left hand
[L1856] European-style (Army habit), eyes on the dataslate. Second meal between 2000 and 2200,
[L1857] similar. She does not eat breakfast. She does not eat at table with company except under
[L1858] directorate-function obligation.

[L1860] Preferences. Strongly proteinous, carbohydrate-moderate, salt-tolerant. She will eat anything
[L1861] operational requirements present and complains about none of it. Off-duty she has been
[L1862] observed to order the same thing — grilled chicken, rice, green vegetable — from the same
[L1863] three or four restaurants near three or four safehouses. She does not experiment with food.
[L1864] Food is fuel and the menu is a solved problem.

[L1866] Speed. Fast. A meal is twelve to fifteen minutes including walk-time. She has not lingered over
[L1867] a meal on panel in published canon. The one observed exception is a sequence with Fury post-
[L1869] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 46 / 206>[L1870] Secret Invasion — bar food, two hours, the longest meal of her life and possibly the most
[L1871] important.

[L1873] Water. Consistent. She carries a bottle and refills it. Hydration is a discipline.

[L1875] What she will not eat in company. Anything that requires fingers. Anything that risks staining
[L1876] the kit. Anything she would have to look at to manage. She eats with her hands free and her
[L1877] sightlines clear.




[L1882] IX. SUBSTANCE INGESTION
[L1883] Caffeine. Two cups black coffee on rising, one mid-afternoon, occasionally a fourth late-shift.
[L1884] No espresso (volume insufficient to sustain hydration). Tea on the rare days she is recovering
[L1885] from a hangover.

[L1887] Alcohol. The defining substance, behaviorally. Pattern: solo, in quarters or in a single specific
[L1888] dive bar she has used for a decade, after operationally compromising decisions. Drink of
[L1889] choice: brown liquor, neat, served in a regulation tumbler she has used long enough that the
[L1890] etching on the base has worn through. Pours are heavy and uncounted; she does not measure.
[L1891] Two to four pours on a normal bad night; five-plus on the nights she has lied to a friend.

[L1893] She does not drink in company except ceremonial (a toast at a wake) and does not drink to
[L1894] intoxication-visible-to-others. The drinking is private and is deliberately invisible to the chain of
[L1895] command, which knows about it anyway. She does not drink in the field. She does not drink
[L1896] within twelve hours of a deployment. She believes the discipline around the drinking is what
[L1897] proves the drinking is not a problem; an honest review of the volume would conclude otherwise.

[L1899] Nicotine. None. She does not smoke and never has.

[L1901] Pharmaceuticals. Ibuprofen for the body. The sleep aids she has been prescribed go unused
[L1902] — she does not trust the loss of vertical-recovery window they would require. She has refused
[L1903] on-record psychological pharmacotherapy from SHIELD medical on three documented
[L1904] occasions, citing operational fitness review concerns; the actual reason is that she will not be
[L1905] that legible.




[L1910] X. INTIMACY & SEXUAL SOMATICS
[L1911] Baseline. Effectively closed. No on-panel relationship of duration. No spouse, no partner, no
[L1912] dependents. Whether this reflects orientation, opportunity, deliberate election, or all three is
[L1913] undetermined from the record; what is determined is that she has organized her physical life so
[L1915] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 47 / 206>[L1916] that intimacy is structurally inaccessible — there is no time, no residence, no off-duty self for a
[L1917] partner to know.

[L1919] Touch tolerance. Low in baseline, calibrated by trust. She does not initiate handshakes; she
[L1920] returns them firmly and briefly. Shoulder-claps from Fury are received without flinch but also
[L1921] without return. She does not hug. The few times she has been hugged (an emotional
[L1922] subordinate post-survival; Pepper Potts post-extraction) she has held still rather than
[L1923] reciprocated, hands at her sides, jaw set, until the contact ended.

[L1925] Touch she initiates. Operational only — a hand to a subordinate's shoulder to steer them
[L1926] through a door, a palm at the small of a wounded teammate's back to support weight, fingers at
[L1927] a casket lid (§III). The contact is always purposive and always brief.

[L1929] Erotic register. Inferred, sparse. The Bendis-era Stark antagonism contains a charge that both
[L1930] parties refuse to act on for years; whether it ever resolves in the published record is ambiguous
[L1931] and probably deliberately so. Whatever sexual life she conducts is conducted off-page, on her
[L1932] own terms, with strict containment from operational life. The behavioral profile predicts brief,
[L1933] infrequent, transactional contact with vetted partners — likely other operators or former
[L1934] operators — and no continuity. She would not allow someone to stay the night in a quarters she
[L1935] sleeps armed in.

[L1937] Intimacy as it actually appears. Not sexual. The closest thing to intimacy in the record is the
[L1938] two-hour bar meal with Fury, the silent ride home with Stark after the extraction, the moment
[L1939] she stood at Rogers' shoulder when no one else would — proximity, sustained, with someone
[L1940] who knows what she knows and does not require her to perform anything. This is what intimacy
[L1941] looks like for her: shared weight, no words, the body present and the guard partially down.




[L1946] XI. STATE-DEPENDENT SUMMARY MATRIX
[L1947] Calm. Posture loaded but loose. Blink rate 15/min. Breath slow. Right-corner mouth-pull
[L1948] occasionally active. Hands at belt or seam. Voice at trained register, 140 wpm.

[L1950] Cognitive load (reading a bad report, sitting through a directorate brief). Bridge gesture
[L1951] appears. Hair-tuck on the right. Jaw-clench visible. Blink rate drops to 10–12/min. Respiration
[L1952] unchanged. Voice unchanged in public, lower and quieter when alone.

[L1954] Operational stress (active op, command seat). Sentences shorten. Voice pitch flattens. Heel-
[L1955] strike returns to gait as she moves the deck. Earpiece-check frequency rises. Folder-tap
[L1956] becomes more emphatic. Pupils run wide. The metronome holds.

[L1958] Threat (weapon out, hostile in close). Color leaves the face. Blink rate near zero. Right hand
[L1959] goes still on grip or table. Breath: four-in, six-out. She does not speak unless speaking is the
[L1961] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 48 / 206>[L1962] tactical action. The body is fully forward of the hips and the strong-side knee is unlocked.

# PDF Skill (Read • Inspect • Extract • Edit • Render • Forms • OCR • Redact • Convert • Diff)

This skill is designed for **reliable, workflow-driven** PDF work: **render -> verify -> operate -> re-render verify**.

## Before you touch PDFs: should this be DOCX/PPTX instead?

Even if the user asks for a PDF deliverable, the best workflow is often:

- **Text-heavy, business-doc layout (headings, TOC, long tables, rich lists)** -> use the **DOCX skill** to author, then convert to PDF with `lo_convert_to_pdf.py`.
- **Slide-like visual layout (charts, callouts, fixed positioning, figure captions)** -> use the **Slides skill** (PPTX) to author, then export to PDF.
- **Programmatic generation** -> ReportLab (this skill) is fine.

If you find yourself hand-tuning line breaks or typography in ReportLab, you probably picked the wrong authoring format.

---
## Core loop (always)

1) Render to images

```bash
python /home/oai/skills/pdfs/scripts/render_pdf.py input.pdf --out_dir /mnt/data/_renders/in --dpi 200
```

2) Inspect PNGs (tables/figures/layout are authoritative)

3) Perform the edit/extract/create

4) Re-render and compare

```bash
python /home/oai/skills/pdfs/scripts/compare_renders.py before.pdf after.pdf --out_dir /mnt/data/_diff --dpi 200
```

## Design standards for document generation

For generating new documents or major rewrite/repackages, follow the design standards below unless the user explicitly requests otherwise. The user's instructions always take precedence; otherwise, adhere to these standards.

When creating the document design, do not compromise on the content and make factual/technical errors. Do not produce something that looks polished but not actually what the user requested.

It is very important that the document is professional and aesthetically pleasing. As such, you should follow this general workflow to make your final delivered document:

1. Before you make the PDF, please first think about the high-level design of the PDF:
   - Before creating the document, decide what kind of document it is (for example, a memo, report, SOP, workflow, form, proposal, or manual) and design accordingly. In general, you shall create documents which are professional, visually polished, and aesthetically pleasing. However, you should also calibrate the level of styling to the document's purpose: for formal, serious, or highly utilitarian documents, visual appeal should come mainly from strong typography, spacing, hierarchy, and overall polish rather than expressive styling. The goal is for the document's visual character to feel appropriate to its real-world use case, with readability and usability always taking priority.
   - You should make documents that feel visually natural. If a human looks at your document, they should find the design natural and smooth. This is very important; please think carefully about how to achieve this.
   - Think about how you would like the first page to be organized. How about subsequent pages? What about the placement of the title? What does the heading ladder look like? Should there be a clear hierarchy? etc
   - Would you like to include visual components, such as tables, callouts, checklists, images, etc? If yes, then plan out the design for each component.
   - Think about the general spacing and layout. What will be the default body spacing? What page budget is allocated between packaging and substance? How will page breaks behave around tables and figures, since we must make sure to avoid large blank gaps, keep captions and their visuals together when possible, and keep content from becoming too wide by maintaining generous side margins so the page feels balanced and natural.
   - Think about font, type scale, consistent accent treatment, etc. Try to avoid forcing large chunks of small text into narrow areas. When space is tight, adjust font size, line breaks, alignment, or layout instead of cramming in more text.

Up Front. All assessments evidence-derived; substantiation in following sections.




1. BOTTOM LINE — ONE PARAGRAPH
Maria Hill is a thirty-something former U.S. Army officer who has organized her entire adult
existence around a single proposition: that she is worth precisely what she is useful for, and the
heavier the load she can carry without complaint, the closer she gets to being enough. She is a
brunette, blue-eyed, peak-conditioned but unaugmented woman who has chosen to spend her
working life in rooms with literal gods, holding extinction-tier secrets in a body that can be killed
by a single bullet — and has been. She is not ambitious in the careerist sense; she has
accepted demotion without grievance and refused promotion when the chair came with the
wrong flag on it. She is not warm, and not because she cannot be — because warmth feels, to
her, like the tell that gets you killed or replaced. The through-line from a contemptuous Chicago
father to an unmarked Helicarrier office is unbroken: find the room where being unloved is the
price of admission, and become indispensable to it. She is, by any honest reading, one of the
most competent intelligence officers in her world and one of the loneliest. Both facts are the
same fact.




2. THE THROUGH-LINE
Trace the spine of the life and a single curve appears:

    Child in a household where a father could not be satisfied and a mother died before she
    could be a counterweight — the formative lesson being love is contingent on performance
    and performance is never sufficient.
    Adolescent who, given a brother who answered the same wound by going into the
    priesthood (a different absolute institution, a different uniform, the same surrender of
    personal life to a larger order), answers it by going into the Army.
    Officer who, in a military that rewards exactly the temperament her father drilled into her —
    clipped affect, procedural fidelity, contempt for excuse-making — finds for the first time that
   the shape of her interior reads to others as virtue.
   S.H.I.E.L.D. recruit and rapid riser who is promoted not on charisma (she has none of the
   kind that wins rooms) but on metrics, reliability, and political non-threat — and who is
   installed over Nick Fury's chair specifically because she carries no legacy, no relationships,
   no war stories that would let her resist civilian oversight.
   Director under fire who walks into a building of operators that openly resent her and
   answers the resentment by enforcing regulation harder, not softer — overcorrecting in
   exactly the direction that confirms the resentment, because under-correcting would prove
   her father right.
   Hunted fugitive during the Osborn ascendancy who refuses to keep the chair when the
   chair turns Hydra-adjacent, goes underground at the cost of her career and body, and
   entrusts her life to a man (Stark) she had spent years antagonizing — because the
   operational logic of who could hide her overrode the relational logic of who would want to.
   Deputy Director and Illuminati confidant who, returned to the apparatus, accepts a
   permanent demotion without grievance and absorbs the burden of knowing about
   Incursions, Rogers' mind-wipe, and antimatter contingency without participating in the
   decisions or sharing the weight with anyone she did not have to.
   Executed officer who is shot point-blank by a Hydra-corrupted Captain America and, on
   resurrection, returns to the same chair, the same hours, the same bottle, the same posture.

The curve never bends. The wound is never reopened in a way that lets it heal; it is only re-
armored. What changes across the decades is not the wound — it is the sophistication of the
load-bearing structure she builds over it. The early Hill (Bendis era) is rigid; the later Hill
(Hickman, Spencer) is practiced. Same compensation, more tradecraft.

The wound: I am only as valuable as I am useful, and even at maximum usefulness I will not
be loved.

Source: A father who modeled withholding as discipline and contempt as feedback, in a

to the chain of command. Both children sought a hierarchy strict enough that performance could
substitute for relationship.

Maintenance — how she keeps the wound exactly where it is, neither healed nor lethal:

 1. Environmental selection. She lives and works in institutions (Army, S.H.I.E.L.D., the

 5. Doctrinal cover. She has constructed an explicit operational philosophy — civilians get to

taking the job away, forcing unstructured time, putting her in a room where competence is not

Chronology IV — Recent History & Current State
Dossier section. Subject: HILL, Maria (Cmdr.). Time-window: post-resurrection through present

4.1 The Return — Re-Entry After Execution
The operational fact at the spine of this period is that the subject was killed by a point-blank
gunshot to the head during the Hydra occupation (Secret Empire #10) and subsequently
restored to life. No file on Hill written after this event can pretend the event did not occur.
Restoration of biological function is not restoration of the person; the literature on operators who
survive near-execution (let alone actual execution) is uniformly clear that the post-event subject
is a structurally altered version of the pre-event subject, and the behavioral record bears this
out.

The first ninety days post-restoration. The subject did not request, and was not granted,
extended decompression leave. She returned to active rotation within what intelligence-
medicine doctrine would call a clinically inadvisable window — by inference, under three weeks
from re-animation to first verified operational signature. Her stated rationale (per Strikeforce and
adjacent appearances) is the same rationale she has used for every prior re-entry from injury:
the desk doesn't fill itself. The actual rationale, derived from her established pattern, is that
unstructured convalescent time is the single environmental condition she is least equipped to
tolerate. To sit still after dying would have required her to feel having died.

Physiological residue. A through-skull GSW, even with full restoration, leaves predictable
somatic tells: occasional left-side temporal headaches under fatigue load (inferred from her
observed late-shift retreat to dimmed lighting and the visible jaw-clench during prolonged
briefings); a heightened acoustic startle threshold, paradoxically narrower rather than wider —
she has trained the flinch out, but the autonomic spike still registers in micro-expression for a
fraction of a second before suppression. Sleep architecture is degraded. She is observed (or, in
the file convention, would be observed) waking between 0340 and 0420 with high consistency,
three to five nights per week — the classic mid-cycle cortisol-spike pattern of chronic
operational stress overlaid on traumatic event memory.

Psychological residue. She has not spoken about the execution to any party on panel. This is
consistent with her lifelong defensive structure (compartmentalization, reaction formation
against warmth) and should not be read as evidence of integration. The absence of disclosure
is the symptom. Her drinking, per the established pattern, has not increased in volume so much
as in regularity — the pour is the same; the nights without a pour are fewer.




4.2 Current Institutional Position
Title and reporting line. Deputy Director, with operational latitude exceeding her nominal
grade — the consequence of a decade in which she has been the de facto Director whenever
Fury is off-grid (which is most of the time) and the institutional memory whenever the
surrounding directorate has been killed, replaced, infiltrated, or politically defenestrated (which
is most of the time). She is, in plain language, the person who knows where every file is, and
the person whose signature most often appears on the carbon copy below the Director's.

The chair she sits in. SHIELD as an organization has been dissolved, reconstituted, infiltrated,
and rebranded enough times in her tenure that the loyalty-to-institution frame from her early
years requires updating. She is no longer loyal to SHIELD as a name on a wall; she is loyal to
the function — to the existence of a serious adult intelligence apparatus that stands between
civilians and extinction-tier threats, by whatever current acronym. This is a meaningful
evolution. The early Hill would have died for the seal. The current Hill would, and has, walked
away from the seal to preserve the function (the Osborn refusal was the prototype; she has
repeated the pattern at smaller scale several times since).

Operational portfolio, present-day. By inference from the latest published rotation, her
standing portfolio includes: (a) Avengers-adjacent crisis liaison — the person heroes call when
a problem requires a Helicarrier and a manifest; (b) black-tier counterintelligence against
residual Hydra cells and successor organizations; (c) custodianship of the post-Illuminati secret
inventory (what Rogers was made to forget, what the antimatter contingency planning included,
what survived the multiversal reset in operational memory); and (d) recruitment and vetting of
the next-generation operator class, a task she resists in conversation and executes

Wake. 0500 nominal; 0340–0420 involuntary on a majority of nights, with a deliberate non-
engagement protocol (do not check the phone, do not get up, do not concede) before
secondary sleep onset around 0445 and alarm-driven rise at 0500.

First sixty minutes. Black coffee, two cups, no food. PT — the Army-derived calisthenic-and-
run circuit she has used since her twenties, modified for whatever space the current platform
provides. Shower. Uniform.

Uniform discipline. Tactical command gear, dark, fitted, no insignia visible beyond what
regulation requires. Hair pulled back to operational length on duty; loosened to shoulder only in
quarters. Sidearm worn at all times on platform, including in mess. She does not carry it for
threat — she carries it because the weight of it on her hip is part of how she knows who she is.

Morning intelligence cycle. 0600 SCIF briefing, standing, no chair offered or taken. She reads
the overnight take from three sources before allowing the analyst to speak, and she remembers
what was in yesterday's, which is the small terror she cultivates in her staff. She asks one or
two questions, both surgical. She does not soften the delivery. The analysts who survive the
first month learn to come in over-prepared and under-emotive, and the ones who do are, almost
without exception, the ones she quietly advances.

Mid-day. Operational coordination, signature traffic, vetting reads. She eats at her desk —
protein, the same three or four rotating items, no ceremony. She does not lunch with peers.
Invitations are declined with a stock phrase ("I'm buried"); the phrase is sometimes true and
sometimes a habit.

Afternoon. The harder conversations. Phone calls with field assets, with allied directors, with
the occasional Avenger who needs something only she can authorize. Her voice on these calls
is half a register lower than her briefing voice and noticeably drier — the version of her that the
operators trust, which is not the version the analysts see.

Evening. Personnel paperwork, the work she most resents and most reliably completes. She
signs the letters to families of the killed by hand. She does not delegate this. She has done it for
over a decade and the file would contain, if anyone collected them, hundreds of her signatures
on hundreds of envelopes.

Late evening / decompression. Quarters. Boots off, holster off, hair down. Two fingers of
whatever brown spirit is current — bourbon by long preference, occasionally an Irish whiskey
when the bourbon runs out. One pour, occasionally two, almost never three. She reads —
actual paper, not screens — reliably non-fiction, often military history or biography (the
comparison set she runs herself against), occasionally a re-read of a novel she liked in her
twenties. She does not watch entertainment. She has no streaming subscription under any
known name. The television in her quarters, when there is one, runs muted news.

Sleep. Lights out by 2300 on a disciplined night; later when the work demands. She sleeps on
her back, sidearm in the drawer within reach. The drawer is opened, not closed, when she goes
to bed — a tell from the Osborn pursuit years that has never been retired.




4.4 Relational Map, Present-Day
Fury. Off-grid more than on. Their communication is sparse, encrypted, and characterized by
the dry mutual respect of two people who have worked together long enough to leave most
things unsaid. He is the closest thing to a peer she has. She would not call him a friend; she
would, if pressed, allow that there is no one in the world she would rather have at her back. The
asymmetry — that he has many such people and she has him — is not a thing she examines.

Rogers. Complicated by the layered history of secret-keeping (his mind-wipe, his Hydra
impersonation, her own execution by the Hydra version). Functional working relationship
restored; subterranean wariness intact on both sides. She respects him more than she trusts
him, which is, by her standards, a significant amount of respect.

Stark. The longest-running professional relationship in which her armor has been visibly partial.
The Osborn extraction welded something into place that neither of them names. Current contact
is intermittent and warm by her standards — meaning: she will pick up his calls without
checking who it is, and she will occasionally call him without an operational pretext, which from
her is the equivalent of a love letter from anyone else.

The Avengers roster, broadly. Cool professional. She knows their files better than they know
themselves. She has opinions about each of them which she does not share. She has, over
time, developed a quiet protectiveness toward several — Natasha (operator-recognizes-
operator), Carol (Air Force–Army professional kinship), the younger generation she vets —
which she expresses exclusively through resource allocation and never through speech.

The brother. Still in the priesthood, by inference still estranged in any meaningful sense, still
the recipient of a holiday card per year that says nothing and is signed Maria. He keeps them.
She does not know that.

The father. Deceased or as good as. If living, uncontacted. The wound is intact precisely
because it was never closed.

Romantic. None on record. None inferred. The architecture of her life is structurally
inhospitable to it and she has not, in any depicted window, attempted to renovate the
architecture. This is not a deprivation she experiences as deprivation; it is a condition she
experiences as the price of the chair, and she has long since stopped itemizing the bill.




4.5 The Current Threat Environment
She is operating in a period in which the threat menu has expanded faster than the institutional
response capacity. Hydra successor cells, multiversal incursion residue, AI-enabled non-state
actors, the perennial cosmic-tier intrusions, and the slow-burning problem of superhuman
political organization at scales that exceed any single nation's regulatory reach — all of these
cross her desk. She manages the load by triage and by the same compartmentalization that
has kept her functional for fifteen years.
The novel pressure of the present period is succession. She is no longer the youngest serious
operator in the room. The next generation is arriving — analysts, field operators, the occasional
super-powered recruit — and she is being asked, implicitly and explicitly, to build the bench.
This is work she is constitutionally suited for (she will be a relentless, fair, terrifying mentor) and
emotionally evasive about (because to train a successor is to admit that one will, eventually, be
succeeded, and the chair is the thing holding her together).




4.6 Present State — Synthesis
She is, at this moment in her chronology, the most operationally capable version of herself she
has ever been. She is also the most quietly attenuated. The execution did not break her; it
confirmed, at the cellular level, the bargain she made in her twenties — that the self is what
survives the job, and the job is what the self is for. She has not grieved her death because to
grieve it would require an interior life she has not maintained the infrastructure for. She has not
celebrated her return because there is no one she would celebrate with whose celebration
would not feel like exposure.

She wakes early. She drinks her coffee. She reads the take. She signs the letters. She pours
the two fingers. She opens the drawer. She sleeps on her back. She is forty-something, alive, in
command, alone in the specific way that operators of her grade are alone, and she is — by
every metric that matters to her and by no metric that would matter to anyone trying to love her
— exactly where she intended to end up.

The file remains open. The subject remains, in the precise sense of the word, on station.

End Chronology IV. Continue to subsequent module.

Attachment & Relational Patterns
ATTACHMENT & RELATIONAL PATTERNS
UATU dossier, Section 6. Cross-referenced against the full behavioral record from New
Avengers #4 (2005) through Strikeforce (2019–2020). All inferences substantiated from on-
panel conduct; granular extrapolation flagged as such.




6.1 The Originating Attachment Environment
The relational template was set in a Chicago row house before she was twelve.

The father — never named on panel, present in Reed's 2008 one-shot as a man whose
approval was structured as a permanent withholding — is the architect. He is not a beater; he is
worse than that for the formation of a Maria Hill. He is a man who responds to a child's offered
achievement with a recalibrated standard. Bring home an A and the next conversation is about
the A+. Make varsity and the conversation is about starting. There is no terminal state of
"enough" in his economy, because the function of "not enough" is to keep the child oriented
toward him. The withholding is the bond.
The mother dies young. The exact mechanism is unspecified in canon; the consequence is
specified by everything Hill does afterward. She loses, before her attachment system has
finished wiring, the one figure who might have modeled unconditional regard. What remains is a
household of two males — the contemptuous father, the brother who will later flee into the
priesthood — and a girl who learns the only available currency is performance.

The brother's vocational choice is a piece of evidence Hill's file should not gloss. He went
toward a structure that promised absolute, unconditional love from a non-human source — a
father who, by doctrinal definition, cannot withhold. She went toward a structure that promised
conditional approval from an institution that would always demand more. The siblings made
opposite peaces with the same wound. They do not, so far as canon shows, speak.

Resulting attachment classification. Dismissive-avoidant, with a secondary disorganized
streak around figures of paternal authority. She does not score as anxious-preoccupied (no
clinging, no protest, no pursuit). She does not score as fearful-avoidant in the classic sense
(she is not afraid of closeness so much as untrained in it). The diagnostic tell is what she does
when she's hurt: she goes quieter, not louder; she withdraws to a room with a door and a bottle;
she does not call.




6.2 The Bonding Algorithm
Hill does not bond the way most people bond. She does not exchange disclosures, share food
rituals, mark anniversaries, or accumulate inside jokes. She bonds through a slower, more
idiosyncratic process best described as load-bearing trust accretion.

The sequence, observable across every significant relationship in her record:

 1. Adversarial first contact. She arrives clipped, procedural, mildly antagonistic. The other
   party is required to either match her competence or stop wasting her time. Stark, Rogers,
   Wolverine, Danvers, Rogers-again-after-Hydra, Coulson in the Hickman runs — all met her
   this way and all initially disliked her. This is not a strategy; it is the only opening register she
   has.
 2. A weight test. Somewhere in the relationship's first arc there is a moment where the other
   party is asked, often without knowing it's a test, to carry something heavy and not flinch.
   Stark passes by hiding her under Resilient's roof while she's bleeding. Rogers passes by
   absorbing operational intelligence without leaking it. Fury passed long ago by handing her
   the chair and letting her be hated for sitting in it. People who flinch are quietly demoted in
   her interior org chart. They are not cut off — she is too professional for that — but they are
   reassigned to a relational tier from which they will not be promoted.
 3. Silent reclassification. The bond, once formed, is not announced. There is no scene in
    which Hill tells Stark she now considers him a friend. There is, instead, a scene three issues
    later in which she rolls her eyes at him with a particular familiarity that wasn't there before
    — a microexpression upgrade. The recipient knows. Almost no one else does.
 4. Loyalty as substrate. Once bonded, she will absorb structural cost — career, body,
    freedom, life — on the bonded party's behalf without renegotiation. The Stark hard-drive
    extraction is the prototype. She is shot multiple times running it. She does not, before,
    during, or after, ask for or accept gratitude beyond a nod.

The algorithm produces very few bonds and very strong ones. Her interior org chart,
reconstructed from a decade of panel evidence, contains perhaps six names with full clearance
and perhaps fifteen with partial. Everyone else is staff.




6.3 The Distrust Architecture
Distrust is her default. Trust is the deviation that requires evidence. This inverts the civilian
baseline, and the inversion is operationally adaptive — she has worked in rooms where the
person next to her was a Skrull, a Hydra plant, an LMD, or a mind-controlled friend. The
professional paranoia is calibrated to ground truth.

The architecture has layers:

    Procedural distrust (everyone, always): the assumption that any given person in the
    building may be compromised, lying, or holding back relevant intelligence. This is not
    personal. She extends it to Fury. She extends it to herself — she runs counter-checks on
    her own decisions, audits her own access logs, and (extrapolated from her conduct in the
    Hickman Avengers runs) keeps a private log of her own command judgments to review for
    drift.
    Operational distrust (everyone she has not weight-tested): the assumption that a given
    collaborator will, under stress, optimize for something other than the mission. This is the
    layer that gets the Avengers their initial Hill experience. It is removable; it requires
    demonstrated reliability across at least one bad day.
    Relational distrust (everyone, including those who have passed both prior layers, with
    respect to her interior life): the assumption that disclosing emotional content creates a
    vulnerability the other party may, without meaning to, eventually use. This layer almost
    never gets removed. Fury does not get through it. Stark does not get through it. The closest
    anyone gets is a Hickman-era scene where she allows Steve Rogers to see that she is
    tired. The whole exchange is three lines.
The architecture has one critical bug, well-documented across the record: it does not
distinguish well between threat to the mission and threat to herself. She does not perform self-
protective distrust. When she goes underground from Osborn, the strategic logic is sound but
the personal logic is missing — she does not consider extraction abroad, does not consider
retirement, does not consider any future in which Maria Hill exists outside of SHIELD. The
distrust that would protect her self is unbuilt because the self has been fused into the institution.
(See §4 on institutional fusion as substitute paternal object.)




6.4 Betrayal — Received and Given
Received. Hill's record of being betrayed is long and forms much of her file's emotional spine.

Fury's Latverian incursion (her installation context) was not a betrayal of her but it shaped her
— she inherited his bed, his enemies, and his unfinished operational debts, and she was given
no warm-up time. Osborn's takeover after Secret Invasion is the cleanest betrayal-by-system:
the framework she had served promoted her enemy and made her a fugitive. Hydra's hollowing
of SHIELD across multiple runs is the chronic betrayal — the discovery, over and over, that the
institution she fused with was rotten in segments she had unknowingly enabled.

Her response to received betrayal is diagnostic. She does not rage. She does not grieve
openly. She recalibrates the threat model. After Osborn she works for Stark in exile and never
publicly relitigates the displacement. After each Hydra reveal she does a quiet internal purge
and does not write a memoir. The injury is processed by becoming harder to injure the same
way twice — a pattern that protects against repetition and prevents healing.

Given. Hill betrays, in the technical sense, frequently. She lies to friends as policy in Secret
Avengers, where she wipes her own operatives' memories to protect mission integrity. She
withholds Incursion intelligence from teammates who would benefit from knowing. She runs ops
past Rogers when she has determined Rogers will be operationally counterproductive. She
would describe none of these as betrayals; she would describe them as operational
compartmentalization in service of a duty of care she has not delegated. By her ethic, the
betrayal would be to share the weight and corrupt someone else with it.

This is the most morally fraught seam in her relational style, and she knows it. The solo drinking
clusters around exactly these decisions. She is not at peace with the position; she has simply
not located a better one and refuses to perform peace she does not feel.




6.5 Repair
Hill does not repair the way civilians repair. There is no apology scene in her file. There is no
"we should talk about what happened." Repair, for her, happens through one of three
mechanisms:

 1. Resumed function. The relationship is restored by both parties returning to operational
    collaboration without comment. The grievance is allowed to exist; it is simply demoted
    beneath the work. Most of her major relationships are stabilized this way. After she draws
    on Stark in Secret Invasion #1, the next several arcs do not include a conversation about it;
    they include her risking her life for him.
 2. Demonstrated cost-bearing. When she has injured someone she actually cares about,
    she pays the debt in a currency they will recognize without her naming it. She runs the
    dangerous op. She takes the round. She covers the leak. The repair is the act; the act is the
    apology. To anyone watching for verbal contrition, no repair has happened. To the recipient,
    who has worked in the same world long enough to read the dialect, repair has happened in
    the only register that means anything.
 3. The dry acknowledgment. Once or twice a decade, with one of the six fully-cleared
    names, she will produce a single sentence of unalloyed regard — usually wrapped in irony,
    delivered without eye contact, often at the end of an operation where someone nearly died.
    The Hickman runs contain at least two such moments with Fury. They are the closest she
    comes to language for any of this.

She does not pursue repair from people she has demoted. If a colleague has flinched at a
weight test and the relationship has been quietly reassigned, she does not work to recover it.
The energy required would be net-negative against the mission. This is one of the colder
elements of her style, and people on the receiving end of it correctly perceive a closed door.




6.6 Intimacy and Dependency
The intimacy file is nearly empty, and the emptiness is itself the data.

There is no on-panel romantic relationship of any sustained duration across the entirety of her
canonical record. There are flickers — the Bendis-era flirtation banter with Stark that is largely
his initiative and largely her deflection; an arguable subtext with Coulson in some Hickman-
adjacent material; the kind of professional intimacy with Fury that has been read as romantic by
readers but is, on the page, paternal-substitutive. None of it consolidates. None of it produces a
partner.

This is not asexuality and it is not, in the clinical sense, avoidance of sex specifically. It is
avoidance of the relational architecture sex would require her to build. A partner would have to
be allowed into the schedule, the residence she does not really keep, the interior weather she
does not share. A partner would create a person whose well-being she would have to factor into
operational calculus — and the calculus is already running at maximum load. A partner would
be a vulnerability that the threat model could not adequately contain. Her solution is to not have
one.

Dependency. She refuses it. The dismissive-avoidant signature is clearest here. She does not
ask for help; when she needs it, she frames the ask operationally ("I need a safehouse," not "I
am afraid"). She does not allow herself to be cared for in any register that would require her to
be visibly weak. The Osborn arc, when she is shot and on the run, is the closest the record
comes — and even there, she frames her presence at Stark's as a tactical asset to his
situation, not an admission of need in hers.

The cost of this is somatic. She carries chronic stress load that a healthier relational system
would partially metabolize through being known. She drinks alone instead. The drinking is not a
vice; it is the structural consequence of refusing dependency in a job that generates more
weight than a single nervous system can carry.




6.7 The Template, Repeated
Across every significant relationship in her file, the same template runs:

   Arrive cold. Do the job. Let them dislike me. Wait for the bad day. See who is still standing
   on the right side of it. Reclassify silently. Carry weight for them without naming the carrying.
   Permit no reciprocation that would require disclosure. Maintain.

With Fury, the template ran across years of subordination; she was reclassified upward after
she did not break under the Director role he abandoned her into. With Stark, the template ran
across the Civil War and Osborn arcs; the gun-draw and the extraction are the two ends of the
same reclassification. With Rogers, the template ran across the SHRA conflict and into the
Hickman secret-keeping; she came to respect him so completely that she did not flinch from
carrying the knowledge of his mind-wipe, which she correctly identified as the heaviest possible
loyalty she could pay him. With Coulson, the template ran in a peer register — two operators
who recognized in each other the same shape of damage and the same refusal to discuss it.
With Danvers in Secret Avengers and adjacent, the template ran adversarially-into-respect, the
standard arc.

The template never ran with her father, because the father had structured the relationship to
make passing the weight test impossible. He moved the line. She has been re-running the test
against substitute paternal objects ever since, and SHIELD — being an institution and not a
person — is the only substitute that does not move the line on her. The job is the only
relationship she has ever fully consummated.
The template never ran with her brother, because he opted out of weight-bearing structures
altogether by choosing a vocation predicated on grace rather than performance. They are
estranged in the specific way that two siblings who made opposite peaces with the same wound
are estranged: not angry, not even sad, simply mutually incomprehensible. Granular
extrapolation, consistent with the record: she sends a Christmas card. He keeps them.

The template, finally, never quite ran with herself. She has not extended to the interior Maria
Hill the patience and accreted trust she extends to the few people who pass her tests. She is, to
herself, perpetually on probation — the weight test never conclude
